#### 1. infantile hypotonia-oculomotor anomalies-hyperkinetic movements-developmental delay syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.454)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6794361)

**Proposed mechanism:** NRXN1 (HGNC:18724) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal cell adhesion and synapse formation (GO:0099530); SYT1 (HGNC:11549) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal cell adhesion and synapse formation (GO:0099530); Neuronal cell adhesion and synapse formation (GO:0099530) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); Neuronal cell adhesion and synapse formation (GO:0099530) —LEADS_TO→ Hypotonia (HP:0001252); Neuronal cell adhesion and synapse formation (GO:0099530) —LEADS_TO→ Oculomotor apraxia (HP:0000576); Neuronal cell adhesion and synapse formation (GO:0099530) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperkinetic movements (HP:0002372). Loss-of-function mutations in NRXN1 and SYT1 both disrupt the crucial pathway of neuronal cell adhesion and synapse formation, leading to a shared set of developmental and neurological phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in NRXN1 exclusively cause developmental delay and hypotonia, while mutations in SYT1 exclusively cause oculomotor anomalies and hyperkinetic movements, without overlap, would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, identification of common pathogenic variants in NRXN1 or SYT1 with a high allele frequency (>1%) in gnomAD would challenge their role as rare disease-causing genes in this context. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NRXN1 and SYT1 in neuronal development could lead to shared therapeutic strategies targeting synaptic function or neuronal connectivity for both disorders.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SHARPIN and the NF-kappaB pathway in these distinct disease entities could reveal novel therapeutic targets for managing inflammatory and immune-related aspects of both conditions, potentially leading to repurposed drugs or novel immunomodulatory therapies.
